description: Multi-facet 3×3 vs single-condition inference cost comparison, based on exp-002 actual GPU timing data
source: exp-002 wall-clock timing from 6 models (Qwen3-8B, Llama, Gemma-2-9B, Mistral, Deepseek-7B, InternLM2.5-7B) on H800/A800 GPUs with vLLM v0.9.2 batch inference, 288 conditions × 200 items = 57,600 evals per model-benchmark pair
gpu_info: Single H800/A800 (94.97 GiB VRAM) per model, vLLM enforce_eager, bfloat16

multifacet_3x3.description: 3 prompts × 3 seeds, D-study optimal for G≥0.80

single_condition.description: 1 prompt × 1 seed, requires more items for equivalent G≥0.80

api_cost_estimate.note: Hypothetical cost if evaluated via commercial API instead of local GPU

summary.key_insight: The 3×3 design uses 2.9× more inference compute (12.7 min vs 4.4 min per model across 5 benchmarks on a single H800 GPU), but requires only 32% as many test items (178 vs 552). Both costs are negligible for 7B models with vLLM batch inference — the entire 3×3 evaluation suite completes in under 13 minutes per model on a single GPU.
summary.when_multifacet_wins: When per-item costs dominate: human annotation of ground truth, manual curation of specialized benchmarks, domain-expert evaluation rubrics, or when items are scarce (e.g., rare languages, niche domains). Also wins when diagnostic value matters — G-theory decomposes variance sources (prompt vs seed vs interaction), enabling targeted mitigation rather than brute-force item scaling.
summary.when_single_wins: When items are freely available (standard benchmarks like MMLU/GSM8K), inference budget is the binding constraint (e.g., evaluating 100+ models in a leaderboard), or when the evaluation infrastructure doesn't support multi-condition scheduling.
summary.practical_recommendation: For typical model evaluation (≤20 models × 5 benchmarks), the 3×3 multi-facet design adds only ~2.8 GPU-hours total overhead versus single-condition. This is a trivial cost for the diagnostic power gained: knowing that prompt variation contributes 15% of score variance (vs seed at 3%) is actionable intelligence that no amount of single-condition testing can provide.

timing_details.note: Per-eval times derived from exp-002 wall-clock timing, averaged across models
timing_details.mc_vs_ff_speedup: MC benchmarks (MMLU/ARC/HellaSwag) are 4-10× faster per eval than free-form (GSM8K/MATH) due to shorter generation length

GSM8K.note: qwen excluded due to run failure

MATH.note: llama/gemma/mistral timing estimated from jsonl timestamps and monitoring log
